method: Compared with the pdftotext text layer of the official PDF (SHA-256 checked) and its official marking scheme.

source.notes: sha256 of the cached sqp.pdf matches source.sha256 exactly. Both sourceUrl and answerSourceUrl are on the official cbseacademic.nic.in domain. Title 'CHEMISTRY (CODE - 043) SAMPLE QUESTION PAPER, CLASS XII (2025-26)', Max Marks 70, Time 3 hours and the 16-page length all match the pack's stated metadata. No printed paper/set code exists on the document, consistent with the pack's note.

questions.reason: Reagent-over-arrow layout linking the chlorobutane starting material to A, B and C is lost in the PDF text layer; the scheme reads as an unordered fragment list as printed, even though the officialAnswer (verified against the marking scheme) is correct.
questions.notes: MS page 1 confirms A=but-1-ene, B=butan-2-ol (Markovnikov), C=butan-1-ol (anti-Markovnikov via hydroboration); option C matches.
Λ°m rebuilt from math-italic Unicode glyphs in the PDF; confirmed unambiguous and consistent with the MS derivation.
PDF prints 'Porpanal' (a typo for 'Propanal'); pack's text silently corrects the spelling. Meaning unchanged.

questions.reason: Structures (i)-(iv) referenced by the options are drawn structural formulas on page 4, entirely absent from the text layer; the question can't be answered without them.
questions.notes: MS's garbled '1(2a) B. (iv) and (ii) / (b)' line matches option B's text verbatim, so the stored answer letter is plausible, but the underlying structures still can't be checked.

questions.reason: The reaction energy-profile graph needed to read off enthalpy of reaction and activation energy is a pure image; no numeric values from it appear anywhere in the text layer.
questions.notes: Stored answer (Ea=40 kJ/mol, ΔH=10 kJ/mol) matches the MS text, but neither the question graph nor its values are independently verifiable from the extraction.

questions.reason: Official marking scheme prints '...toluene undergoes free radical substitution of the alkyl group to form benzyl alcohol...' (an apparent typo, since the question's own premise states the product is benzyl chloride); pack's officialAnswer silently changed 'alcohol' to 'chloride' without flagging the deviation from the printed scheme.
questions.notes: MS page 6 (raw and layout modes both) confirms 'benzyl alcohol' is what is actually printed.
Verified independently: Cl-substituted acid is most acidic (lowest pKa), branched isobutyric acid least acidic (highest pKa); matches MS's 'Order of pKa values' line.
MS's answer for all four conversions is entirely reaction-scheme images, not present in the text layer; pack correctly omitted officialAnswer.

The table extraction (Zinc 339, Copper 130) is unambiguous despite the line wrap; this is the deliberate premise of the question (the printed table swaps the real values, since actual atomisation enthalpy of Zn ≈130 and Cu ≈339), matching the MS answer exactly. Pack's own LOW-confidence flag on this item is not warranted.
Balanced equation independently verified for atom and charge balance.

Passage, table and all three question parts match the PDF verbatim. The photo of the conductivity meter ('shown at right') is decorative and not needed to answer any part. The OR-alternative answer (dipped in distilled water) is not present in the standard-version MS text at all; pack reconstructed it from the parallel 'For Visually Challenged' version's MS ('The value will be 0.'), clearly flagged as such -- treated as PARTIAL rather than MATCH.

questions.reason: Part III explicitly directs students to 'Refer to figure 1' for the EDTA structure; that figure and the drawn-structure portion of the answer are images not present in the text layer.
questions.notes: Denticity=6 / 2N+4O donor atoms matches the MS. The officialAnswer's closing line 'EDTA is an electron donor' appears to be carried over from the Visually-Challenged variant's distinct sub-question (b), which the standard version's Part III does not explicitly ask.

Parts II-V match the MS verbatim/near-verbatim. Part I's officialAnswer is correctly flagged as an image not extracted (MS gives no text for it either), hence PARTIAL rather than MATCH; the question itself (draw the structure) is fully specifiable from text.
Parts II-V match the MS verbatim/near-verbatim. Part I's officialAnswer is correctly flagged as an image not extracted.

officialAnswer matches the MS's stated value (Ea≈86.567 kJ/mol) exactly. Independent recomputation of the standard two-point Arrhenius equation with T1=298K, T2=318K, log3=0.4771 gives Ea≈43.3 kJ/mol (the MS's own working appears to divide by (T2-T1)=10 instead of 20, doubling the result); this looks like an error in the official scheme itself, not an extraction error, so the pack's faithful reproduction of the printed value is correctly left uncorrected.

questions.reason: Part I's officialAnswer states 'PT = Pi + x + x = Pi + 2x', which is inconsistent with the official scheme's ICE-table derivation (PT = (Pi-x)+x+x = Pi+x); although the final numeric results (x=50 torr, k≈0.040 s⁻¹) match the official scheme, the shown intermediate equation is incorrect and not what the marking scheme implies.
questions.notes: Part II (Rate=ZAB·e^(-Ea/RT)) matches the MS exactly.
